intro: Compare marks left by a gesture with color that spreads and saturates.
alt: A grid of four painterly treatments with rough pigment, spills, broad color zones and stains in raw canvas.

variants.name: Art Informel
variants.look: An earthy, crusted surface nearly swallows the bust.
variants.history: Art Informel encompassed varied European approaches to spontaneous, materially expressive abstraction after World War II.
variants.when: Let the pressure and weight of the paint carry the picture.
variants.why: Scrapes and ridges register the palette knife’s pressure in every patch.

variants.name: Tachisme
variants.look: Ink-like patches break up the face on a pale ground.
variants.history: Tachisme takes its name from the French tache, meaning a stain or blot, and emphasizes spontaneous marks.
variants.when: Build an image from irregular marks that retain the energy of their placement.
variants.why: Separated marks preserve the individual direction and edge of a gesture.

variants.name: Color Field painting
variants.look: Broad zones of related colors sustain a slowly emerging silhouette.
variants.history: American Color Field painters used expansive areas of color to organize the whole surface.
variants.when: Use scale and neighboring hues to shape how a viewer feels color.
variants.why: Broad neighboring colors register as an enveloping atmosphere rather than local shading.

variants.name: stain painting
variants.look: Diluted color feathers along the fabric instead of sitting in a crest.
variants.history: Helen Frankenthaler’s soak-stain method sent thinned pigment into unprimed canvas and influenced Morris Louis and Kenneth Noland.
variants.when: Let the weave and liquid determine a boundary together.
variants.why: Absorbent fibers allow dilution and capillary action to shape the mark.

source.label: National Gallery of Art · Mountains and Sea

prompt: Draw a single textless art comparison board for a museum-quality online art atlas. Layout is exactly four square cells in 2x2, edge-to-edge, no gutters or borders; precise, strictly equally sized cells. Order is left to right within each row, then next row. Each cell is a distinct style treatment featuring the same female executive from reference, in original new art. The reference image is for identity only: recognizable ash-blonde hair in neat low bun with four-color windowpane hair clip, black-rimmed rectangular glasses over blue eyes, charcoal sheath dress under fitted black blazer, azure pocket square and blue lanyard with blank ID badge, holding a white coffee mug with a little four-color tile mark. Change the actual render style rather than adding only backgrounds. Layout styles in order: Art Informel: coarse, scraped ochre and asphalt-like relief almost obliterates figure; Tachisme: impulsive dark ink patches and splashes on bone-white retain fragments of glasses and hair; Color Field painting: large quiet rectangular zones of glowing magenta and rust frame the figure as a vast hovering soft-edged silhouette; stain painting: dilute pink and turquoise pigment feathers directly into the weave of raw pale canvas around the contour. No readable text, numbers, signatures, words, or extra panels.
